## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(corrplot)

behavior <- read.csv("user_behavior_sample.csv")
head(behavior)

engagement_summary <- behavior %>%
summarise(
avg_pages_viewed = mean(pages_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
avg_time_on_site = mean(time_on_site, na.rm = TRUE),
avg_scroll_depth = mean(scroll_depth, na.rm = TRUE),
conversion_rate = mean(conversion, na.rm = TRUE)
)

engagement_summary

landing_page_analysis <- behavior %>%
group_by(landing_page) %>%
summarise(
sessions = n(),
avg_pages = mean(pages_viewed, na.rm = TRUE),
avg_time = mean(time_on_site, na.rm = TRUE),
conversion_rate = mean(conversion, na.rm = TRUE)
)

landing_page_analysis
ggplot(landing_page_analysis, aes(x = landing_page, y = sessions)) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
labs(x = "Landing Page", y = "Sessions")




exit_analysis <- behavior %>%
group_by(exit_page) %>%
summarise(
exits = n(),
exit_rate = n() / nrow(behavior)
)

exit_analysis

#Conversion Distribution (Pie Chart)
conversion_data <- behavior %>%
count(conversion)

ggplot(conversion_data, aes(x = "", y = n, fill = as.factor(conversion))) +
geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 1) +
coord_polar("y") +
theme_void()
#Time on Site Distribution (Histogram)
ggplot(behavior, aes(x = time_on_site)) +
geom_histogram(bins = 10) +
labs(x = "Time on Site", y = "Frequency")



#Pages Viewed vs Conversion (Box Plot)

ggplot(behavior, aes(x = as.factor(conversion), y = pages_viewed)) +
geom_boxplot() +
labs(x = "Conversion Status", y = "Pages Viewed")

#time on Site vs Pages Viewed (Scatter Plot)
ggplot(behavior, aes(x = time_on_site, y = pages_viewed)) +
geom_point() +
labs(x = "Time on Site", y = "Pages Viewed")


#Correlation Heat map

correlation_matrix <- cor(
behavior[, c("pages_viewed", "time_on_site", "scroll_depth", "conversion")],
use = "complete.obs"
)

corrplot(correlation_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper")


#



```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
